question: What is the act of turning your head and checking your blind spot before changing lanes called?
options: a:An unnecessary practice.,b:A good driving habit.,c:A bad driving habit.
note: Checking blind spots by turning your head over your shoulder before changing lanes, pulling away from a curb, or merging is a good driving habit—you should not rely solely on mirrors.

question: An octagonal road sign is always which of the following?
options: a:A hospital sign.,b:A speed limit sign.,c:A stop sign.
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign always means STOP.

question: Where are you not allowed to park?
options: a:In a driveway if permitted by owner.,b:On private property with permission.,c:In a parking lot.,d:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: Parking is unlawful in locations such as crosswalks or marked bicycle lanes; when parking on the street, be within 12 inches of the curb.

question: What lane width is a motorcycle entitled to use?
options: a:The bicycle lane only.,b:The same full lane width as any other motor vehicle.,c:Only half the width of a regular lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to occupy the full lane, just like other motor vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the driver behind you signals they want to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain your current speed.,b:Slow down to allow room in front of your vehicle for them to pass.,c:Speed up to prevent the pass.
note: When another driver wants to pass, slow down slightly to create space ahead so they can complete the pass safely.

question: To stay safe in poor weather, which of the following should you do?
options: a:Not drive on bald tires.,b:Increase your following distances.,c:Slow down.
note: In poor weather, slow down, increase following distance, and ensure tires have adequate tread for proper control and stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting an oncoming vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.,b:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Pull completely off the road and stop.
note: On narrow roads, allow the oncoming vehicle at least half the main traveled portion so both vehicles can pass safely.

question: When approaching an accident scene, what should you generally do if you are not involved and emergency help has already arrived?
options: a:Stop in the roadway to look.,b:Pull over in the emergency lane and get out to watch.,c:Keep your attention on driving and continue moving.
note: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are involved or assistance is required; keep moving and remain attentive to traffic and pedestrians.

question: On major highways, what driving habits help prevent 'highway hypnosis' and improve safety?
options: a:Keep your eyes fixed on the horizon.,b:Stay alert, keep your eyes moving, and be prepared to react to hazards.,c:Turn off cruise control and close your eyes briefly to rest.
note: To avoid highway hypnosis and stay safe, remain alert, scan the road frequently rather than staring at one spot, and be ready to respond to unexpected hazards.

question: Which of the following should you avoid when driving on slippery roads?
options: a:Reduce your following distance.,b:Always drive at the maximum speed limit.,c:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.
note: Avoid cruise control on slippery roads; reduce speed and increase following distance, and avoid sudden steering or braking.

question: What is the minimum license suspension period for driving without valid liability insurance in Alaska?
options: a:60 days.,b:Two years.,c:90 days.
note: If you are involved in an accident while uninsured or fail to provide proof of insurance within 15 days, your license will be suspended for a minimum of 90 days.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right.,b:Turn your wheels to the left.,c:Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.
note: After checking traffic and signaling, stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the space before beginning your turn to enter the spot.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It reduces engine power slightly but is otherwise harmless.,b:It increases vehicle noise only.,c:It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning in the passenger compartment.,d:It causes a loss of hearing.
note: A leaking exhaust can allow carbon monoxide to enter the vehicle’s cabin; keep the exhaust system free of leaks and repair defects immediately.

question: What causes 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Too much sleep the night before your trip.,b:Frequent rest stops.,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.
note: Highway hypnosis results from staring straight ahead for long periods without actively scanning, which can make you zone out and miss hazards.

question: When stopped for a traffic violation or at an equipment check, what document must the driver produce?
options: a:Proof of insurance.,b:Their driver license.,c:Proof of registration.
note: When stopped, the driver is responsible for providing their driver's license; they should also have registration and proof of insurance available.

question: What does a solid white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:It separates carpool lanes from regular lanes.,b:Traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,c:You may cross whenever you like.,d:Traffic is moving in the same direction and lane changes are discouraged or not allowed.
note: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; a solid white line indicates lane changes are discouraged or forbidden.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do to warn other drivers?
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the travel lane and stand behind it to warn drivers.,b:Sound your horn continuously while stopped on the roadway.,c:Use your four-way emergency flashers and move as far off the road as possible.
note: If your vehicle is disabled, get it safely off the roadway if possible, then turn on hazard flashers and lift the hood to signal trouble.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which checks should you perform before changing lanes on a multilane road?
options: a:Slow down to shrink your blind spot.,b:Honk your horn to alert drivers behind you.,c:Look in your mirrors before staring straight ahead.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors and look over your shoulder to verify the blind spot in the direction you intend to move.

question: As a pedestrian, what is a safe practice when approaching a street or crosswalk?
options: a:Enter a crosswalk at any time because drivers must stop.,b:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching closely.,c:Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles.
note: Pedestrians have right-of-way in crosswalks, but you should not step into the street if vehicles are approaching too closely and cannot stop in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and cannot see because of opposing traffic, you should:
options: a:Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before making the turn.,b:Accelerate quickly across the first clear lane.,c:Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you through.,d:Begin the turn into the nearest lane and then straighten out.
note: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you must cross are clear and you can safely complete the turn.

question: What helps relieve fatigue on a long trip?
options: a:Drive with one eye open at a time.,b:Stop and rest every two hours.,c:Do arm exercises every hour.
note: Take regular breaks—about every two hours—to rest and reduce fatigue; if drowsy, stop driving and rest or sleep.

question: Why must you be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They are more difficult to see than cars.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers than other motorists.,c:They rarely use their headlights.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and easier to miss in traffic and blind spots; it's harder to judge their speed and distance, so drive cautiously around them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Stop before entering any crosswalk.,b:Stop at the stop line when present.,c:Stop before entering the intersection.,d:Continue if the way appears clear.
note: A red traffic light means you must stop before entering the intersection; if present, stop at the stop line or before a crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your destination in heavy city traffic, you should:
options: a:Back up in traffic to reach the destination.,b:Make a sudden U-turn in the road.,c:Stop immediately in the lane.,d:Continue to the next block or use the next legal turn to return.
note: Do not back up or make unsafe maneuvers in heavy traffic; go around the block or use the next legal opportunity to return to your destination.

question: What is true about smoking or preparing to smoke while driving?
options: a:It is recommended on long trips to stay awake.,b:It does not affect driving abilities.,c:It helps you stay alert and improves driving.,d:It is a distracting activity and can reduce driving safety.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke can distract you by taking hands off the wheel and eyes off the road, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns mean?
options: a:You must come to a complete stop before turning.,b:You must merge into the indicated lane.,c:You may turn left if you first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns, but you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Only when the pedestrian follows right-of-way laws.,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.,d:Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against a signal or are otherwise careless.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb instead of into traffic if the brakes fail.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,b:Vehicles in both directions may pass if it is safe to do so.,c:No passing is permitted.
note: A single dashed yellow line separates opposing traffic and indicates passing is permitted when safe.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign usually indicate?
options: a:A public recreation area.,b:A nearby school zone.,c:There is an existing or possible driving hazard ahead.
note: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of existing or potential hazards; they are typically yellow (or orange for temporary work zones).

question: At a railroad crossing where the signals are flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Look for a train,b:Slow down and look for a train.,c:Stop and look for a train.
note: If crossing signals are flashing, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and wait until it is safe to proceed; do not cross while warnings are active.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green light at an intersection allow you to do?
options: a:Slow and prepare to stop.,b:Stop and check oncoming traffic.,c:Turn without yielding to pedestrians.,d:Proceed through when the road is clear.
note: A steady green light means you may drive through the intersection if the way is clear; you may also turn unless a sign prohibits it, but must yield to vehicles and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:By driving off the pavement.,b:If the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: You may pass on the right when the vehicle ahead is waiting to turn left and there is a safe, designated passing lane; you may never pass by driving off the pavement or on narrow bridges.

question: When traveling to an area you don't know well, what should you do before you start driving?
options: a:Depend on road signs to find your way.,b:Begin with only a general idea of your destination.,c:Plan your trip in advance.
note: Plan your trip before you start driving in an unfamiliar area. Don’t begin the trip with only a vague idea of where you are going.

question: Which of the following is a known effect of alcohol on driving?
options: a:Faster,b:Improved coordination.,c:Loss of concentration.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

question: What does a traffic signal showing a solid red arrow require you to do?
options: a:Stop and do not turn in the direction indicated by the arrow until the arrow turns green.,b:Stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.,c:Turn slowly in the direction indicated by the arrow.
note: A solid red arrow prohibits turning in that direction; stop and wait until the arrow changes before making the turn.

question: If convicted of DUI in Alaska, what is the minimum period your license may be revoked?
options: a:30 days,b:60 days,c:At least 90 days
note: A DUI conviction or refusal to take a chemical test results in license revocation for a minimum of 90 days; longer periods may apply depending on circumstances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What action should drivers take when approaching a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Turn on their headlights.,b:Proceed through the intersection with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard; slow down, watch carefully, and proceed when safe.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane mark the edges of a crosswalk. What is true about pedestrian right-of-way in a crosswalk?
options: a:Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians.,b:Pedestrians in crosswalks must be given the right-of-way.,c:No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
note: Marked crosswalks show where pedestrians should cross and drivers must stop for pedestrians who are in the crosswalk.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what precautionary steps should you take?
options: a:Try to drive around any lowered gate if you are in a hurry.,b:Speed up to cross before any gates lower.,c:Look
note: Approach railroad crossings by looking and listening for trains, slowing down, and being prepared to stop until it is safe to cross.

question: Why must you be cautious when passing a bicyclist?
options: a:Because you are traveling faster than the bicycle.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass
note: Cyclists may need to swerve to avoid hazards and oncoming vehicles may not expect you to move into their lane to pass a bicycle, so pass with care.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter an intersection and the traffic light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and back up.,b:Accelerate.,c:Stop as quickly as possible if you can do so safely.
note: When the light turns yellow, slow and stop if you can safely do so; if already in the intersection or too close to stop safely, proceed with caution.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:
options: a:Stay calm and move out of their way.,b:Flash your lights and confront them.,c:Call the police immediately from the roadway.,d:Speed up to retaliate.
note: If cut off by an aggressive driver, remain calm and avoid escalation; get out of their way and keep a safe distance.

question: Why should you pump the brakes on a vehicle that does not have ABS when slowing on a slippery surface?
options: a:To keep air out of the brake line.,b:To prevent the tires from wearing out faster.,c:To help prevent the wheels from locking and avoid skids.
note: On non‑ABS vehicles, pumping the brakes helps prevent wheel lockup and reduces the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces.

question: How should you drive when visibility is reduced by fog?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use high beam headlights to better illuminate the road.,c:Drive cautiously and reduce your speed.
note: Use low beam headlights and slow down in fog; high beams can reflect back and further reduce visibility.

question: What may happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The alcohol will negate the drug’s effects.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both may be increased.,d:They always cancel each other out.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs can intensify impairment; for example, some cold remedies plus alcohol can have stronger effects than expected.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you turn your front wheels when parked facing downhill?
options: a:Pointed straight ahead.,b:Aiming any direction.,c:Turned toward the curb or shoulder.
note: When parked facing downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To reduce the chance of being struck from behind, you should:
options: a:Stop frequently to prevent tailgating.,b:Brake harder than usual to create distance.,c:Keep pace with surrounding traffic within the legal speed limit.,d:Drive noticeably slower than surrounding traffic.
note: Driving with the flow of traffic (within the speed limit) keeps traffic moving smoothly and helps prevent rear-end collisions.

question: How does increasing your vehicle's speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:Decreases your field of vision.,b:Has no effect on vision.,c:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.,d:Increases your field of vision.
note: As speed increases, your field of vision narrows, so you must be more alert to potential hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a multi-lane roadway when you see a Merging Traffic sign, you should:
options: a:Honk at entering traffic to warn them.,b:Stop to let merging cars in.,c:Always maintain your current speed regardless of others.,d:Make room for entering vehicles by moving over if no one is beside you.
note: When there are two or more lanes, make room for merging traffic; if no one is beside you, move over one lane when safe.

question: Under ideal driving conditions, what minimum following distance should you maintain?
options: a:Six seconds.,b:Four seconds.,c:500 feet.
note: Maintain at least a four‑second following distance under ideal conditions; increase the gap when conditions worsen.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels straight.,b:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,c:Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
note: Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left so a rear-end collision won't push you into oncoming traffic; signal your intent.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should your vehicle be positioned when preparing to make a right turn?
options: a:As far to the left as possible.,b:Close to the right side of the street.,c:In the nearest passing lane.,d:Near the center of the street.
note: When making a right turn you should position your vehicle as far to the right side of the road as possible; do not cut across lanes to turn.

question: When you are on a highway divided by two solid yellow lines, when may you cross them?
options: a:Cross under no circumstances.,b:Cross these lines only to make a left turn into or from an alley,c:Cross to pass other vehicles when there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may cross only to make left turns into or from a driveway, alley, or private road.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, how should you return to the road?
options: a:Slow down and very carefully steer back onto the pavement when safe to do so.,b:Brake hard and sharply turn back onto the road.,c:Stop your car on the edge of the road and wait.
note: If your wheels go off the pavement, reduce speed without heavy braking, then carefully steer back onto the roadway when safe.

question: Which of the following best describes a “No zone”?
options: a:A lane with restrictions on speed.,b:The blind spot area around large trucks and buses where smaller vehicles may be unseen.,c:A designated no-passing zone on two-lane roads.
note: “No zones” are the large blind spots around commercial vehicles; avoid lingering in these areas.

question: Which types of drugs can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over-the-counter remedies (all of the above).,b:Only marijuana.,c:Only cold remedies.
note: Many substances—including illegal drugs, prescription medicines, and over-the-counter medications—can impair driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Pedestrian crossing only.,b:Merging traffic ahead.,c:Proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns drivers to proceed with caution and be prepared to stop.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Stay until the police arrive at all costs.,b:Leave immediately since you tried to find the owner.,c:Call your insurance agent and leave.,d:Leave a written notice with your name
note: If you cannot find the owner after striking an unattended vehicle, leave a written notice including your name, address, and circumstances of the accident.

question: Which statement about alcohol’s effect is correct?
options: a:Alcohol does not affect memory.,b:Only long-term heavy drinking affects driving skills.,c:Even a small amount of alcohol can reduce concentration and judgment.,d:Only a BAC greater than the legal limit affects concentration.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair concentration, perception, judgment, and memory, reducing driving ability.

question: What does Alaska require concerning license plates on most vehicles?
options: a:No specific license plate requirement.,b:Two license plates (front and rear).,c:A single license plate mounted on the rear of the vehicle.
note: In Alaska a vehicle generally must display a single license plate on the rear with current month and year tabs; a light should illuminate the plate so it is visible at night.

question: Why is the road often extra slippery during the first half hour of rain?
options: a:Tires have not yet absorbed the water.,b:Dust and oil on the road have not yet washed away.,c:Water tends to pool the most at the beginning of a rainfall.
note: Initial rainfall mixes with oil and dirt on the pavement to form a greasy film, reducing tire traction until washed away.

question: Approaching a school bus with flashing red lights, what must a driver do?
options: a:Stop,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the bus has passed.
note: Drivers must come to a complete stop for a stopped school bus displaying flashing red lights and an extended stop arm; do not attempt to pass.

question: What is the only reliable way to sober up after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Drinking black coffee.,b:Taking a cold shower.,c:Exercising vigorously.,d:Waiting for your body to eliminate the alcohol.
note: Only time will reduce your blood alcohol concentration; coffee, food, or showers do not make you sober.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, you should:
options: a:Force your way into traffic.,b:Assume others will yield to you.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for an opening.
note: Vehicles entering must yield to traffic already on the interstate; merge safely when there is an appropriate gap.

question: Faced with an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, you should:
options: a:Try to squeeze through quickly.,b:Split the difference and pass both at once.,c:Pull onto the shoulder between them.,d:Let the oncoming car pass first
note: When there are multiple hazards, deal with one at a time: let the oncoming car pass, then pass the bicyclist when it is safe to do so.

question: Which of these is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Driving slightly slower than traffic.,b:Using signals consistently.,c:Maintaining a steady lane position.,d:Weaving between lanes.
note: Signs of impaired driving include weaving, erratic speed changes, jerking motions, and sudden stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signals?
options: a:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,b:Changing lanes.,c:Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
note: Use turn signals for any movement left or right, including changing lanes, entering traffic from a parking area or alley, and parking maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic signal shows a green arrow for your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the circular green light appears.,b:Stop,c:Turn in the direction indicated by the arrow when the intersection is clear.
note: A green arrow gives the indicated movement the right-of-way, but you must still watch for pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection.

question: What does the term “No zone” refer to?
options: a:A roadway with volume restrictions on stereos.,b:The large blind spots around a truck or bus.,c:A special speed zone.
note: The “No zone” are the blind spots around large trucks and buses where smaller vehicles may be hidden from the driver's view.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not working because of a power outage, how should you proceed?
options: a:Park and wait in the intersection for power to be restored.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and drive through without stopping.,c:Treat the intersection like a four-way stop and proceed when it is your turn.
note: When signals are out, drivers should yield to others the same as at a four-way stop and proceed with caution when it is their turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle whose driver sounds the horn first.,b:The vehicle approaching from the left.,c:The vehicle approaching from the right.
note: At intersections without signs or signals, you must yield to traffic approaching from your right.

question: Which action helps prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Avoid sudden stops and allow your vehicle to slow before braking.,b:Always check mirrors and blind spots before stopping.,c:Sound your horn before braking.
note: Avoid abrupt stops—release the accelerator to let the car slow, then apply steady brake pressure so drivers behind can react.

question: Which behavior describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Looks out for the actions of other drivers.,b:Drives slowly at all times.,c:Travels at a constant speed.
note: A good defensive driver anticipates other drivers' actions and watches for potential hazards, rather than simply driving slowly or at a fixed speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Proceed without stopping if the intersection is clear.,b:Slow down and continue through without stopping.,c:Come to a complete stop as if at a stop sign
note: A flashing red signal is treated the same as a stop sign: stop completely, yield, and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following must you obey over the others?
options: a:A police officer directing traffic.,b:A steady red light.,c:A stop sign.,d:A flashing yellow light.
note: Directions from authorized traffic officers take precedence over traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a multilane highway, slower traffic should:
options: a:Drive in the left lane.,b:Drive in any lane.,c:Drive in the right lane.,d:Drive on the shoulder to let traffic pass.
note: If you are driving slower than surrounding traffic on a multilane road, use the right lane. The left lane is for faster traffic and passing.

question: When may you legally use parking lights?
options: a:When visibility is poor.,b:Within one hour of sunset or sunrise.,c:When a vehicle is parked.
note: Parking lights may be used only when the vehicle is parked; they are not a substitute for headlights while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.,b:Drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.,c:Stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
note: Stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to pedestrians and approaching vehicles, and do not cross the sidewalk without stopping.

question: Which distraction increases a driver's risk of a crash the most?
options: a:Playing a CD.,b:Listening to the radio.,c:Using a cell phone while driving.
note: Using a cell phone—handheld or hands‑free—or other complex devices increases crash risk significantly.

question: If another car might hit you, what should you do to warn them?
options: a:Turn on emergency lights instead of horn.,b:Wave your arms out the window.,c:Flash your headlights only.,d:Sound your horn.
note: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians when you believe they may not see you and are about to cause a collision.

question: Why must you use extra caution when driving at night?
options: a:Visibility is reduced and you cannot see as well.,b:Traffic moves faster at night.,c:There is more traffic at night.,d:Headlights make it easier to judge distances.
note: Because of darkness, visibility is reduced at night. From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, and whenever persons or vehicles are not visible for 500 feet, headlights are required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which signal indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A steady yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow signal means slow down and proceed with caution; a flashing red is equivalent to a stop sign.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what should you assume?
options: a:The driver may suddenly open a door as you pass, so use extra caution.,b:The driver will wait until you pass, so speed up.,c:The parked car will not move, so slam on your brakes.
note: When passing parked vehicles, assume doors may open or occupants may step out; drive with extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic,b:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed to be driven.,c:Potential driving speeds for the area
note: Speed limit signs indicate the legal maximum or minimum speed under ideal conditions; slow down when conditions require it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you use hand or mechanical turn signals?
options: a:Only after you start the turn.,b:For a minimum of 100 feet before turning or changing lanes.,c:Only in city traffic.,d:Only when there is traffic behind you.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before a turn or lane change; longer signals are required at higher speeds.

question: What do orange-colored road signs typically indicate?
options: a:The start of a no passing zone.,b:Construction or maintenance work ahead.,c:A school zone is ahead.,d:A railroad crossing ahead.
note: Orange signs are used for construction, maintenance, and emergency operations and warn drivers of work zones or related hazards.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:All railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.,b:You never need to stop for a crossing.,c:It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
note: You must obey gates, signs, and flaggers at crossings; it is illegal and dangerous to go around lowered gates, and not all crossings have signals or gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When entering a street from a garage or alley.,b:When your traffic signal is a green arrow.,c:When they are on a road to your left and you have reached an unmarked intersection at the same time.
note: Yield to traffic and pedestrians when entering a street from a driveway, garage, or alley, and yield to the right at unmarked intersections when arriving simultaneously.

question: To help prevent crashes, you should:
options: a:Never use your horn.,b:Ignore other drivers on the road.,c:Communicate your intentions with other road users.,d:Only drive on back roads to avoid traffic.
note: Communicate with other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians (signals, lights, horn when appropriate) to reduce surprises and crashes.

question: If you are driving inside another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,b:Keep a steady pace.,c:Stay in the driver's blind spot.
note: Do not drive in someone else's blind spot; move forward or fall back so the other driver can spot you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required at an intersection but there is no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic.,b:You are not required to stop.,c:Only if you can see at least 200 feet on either side.
note: Stop at the point closest to the intersecting roadway where you can get a clear view of approaching traffic without entering the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign indicate?
options: a:The maximum legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:Only a recommended speed.,c:The exact speed to avoid tickets.,d:The minimum required speed.
note: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal driving speed under ideal conditions; you may need to drive more slowly when conditions are poor.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on and is blinding you, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights to warn the other driver.,b:Keep your high beams on until they dim theirs.,c:Glance toward the right side of the road until the vehicle passes.
note: When faced with blinding headlights, look toward the right edge of the road and away from the beams until the vehicle passes to avoid being blinded.

question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Pump the accelerator repeatedly.,b:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,c:Drive faster to get past puddles quickly.,d:Slow down and make sure tires are properly maintained.
note: Reduce speed when roads are wet, watch for standing water, and keep tires in good condition to reduce the risk of hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to an emergency vehicle using sirens or flashing lights?
options: a:When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.,b:Only if the emergency vehicle is behind you.,c:Only when other drivers yield first.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle that is using audible or visual signals.

question: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, when should you proceed after a train passes?
options: a:Start across as soon as the first train passes.,b:Follow the car ahead immediately regardless of view.,c:Cross quickly without looking.,d:Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks.
note: Do not move until you have a clear view along all tracks; another train may be approaching on a different track.

question: When near a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Force the motorcycle to give up lane position.,b:Allow the motorcycle a full lane to itself.,c:Share half of your lane with the motorcycle.,d:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles and need a complete lane; give them the full lane width to maneuver safely.

question: When passing a bicyclist on a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, what is the safest method?
options: a:Slow down until no oncoming traffic is present, then pass while leaving plenty of space.,b:Keep driving; the bicyclist must get out of your way.,c:Wait until the next traffic signal or stop sign to pass.
note: Pass bicyclists as you would other vehicles—slow, ensure clear sightlines, and leave adequate lateral space (typically at least 3 feet).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the common maximum speed limit on most Alaskan roadways unless posted otherwise?
options: a:60 mph.,b:55 mph.,c:50 mph.
note: Unless otherwise posted, many Alaskan roadways have a maximum speed limit of 55 mph; special zones like school or business districts have different limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:The right lane.,b:Either lane.,c:The lane closest to your previous lane.
note: Turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you came from (the nearest lane going in the direction of travel on the one-way street).

question: Which of the following DOES occur after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,b:You become more alert.,c:Your judgment of speed and distance improves.,d:You recover from headlight glare faster.
note: Alcohol reduces reaction time, distorts judgment of speed and distance, reduces alertness, and impairs vision and recovery from glare.

question: A driver approaching a stopped school bus with flashing amber lights must:
options: a:Sound their horn and pass slowly.,b:Slow down and prepare to stop.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the bus has passed.
note: Amber flashing lights indicate the bus is about to stop; slow down and be prepared to stop. Stop when the bus activates flashing red lights and extends the stop arm.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
options: a:Pass with caution.,b:Do not pass.,c:Slow down.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane means passing is not permitted from your direction.

question: On long trips, what is an effective way to prevent drowsiness?
options: a:Slow down and drive more slowly.,b:Turn up the car radio volume.,c:Stop at regular intervals to rest and stretch.
note: Schedule regular stops on long trips to rest and stretch—this helps prevent drowsiness and fatigue.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas.,b:Gradually slow down and pull off the side of the road.,c:Do not immediately use your brakes.
note: Ease off the accelerator, avoid hard braking, gradually slow, and steer to a safe spot to stop before applying brakes.

question: What does a steady yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean you should do?
options: a:Merge into the lane indicated by the arrow.,b:Stop if you can safely do so; a red arrow is coming.,c:You may complete the turn without yielding.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected-turn signal is ending and a red arrow is about to appear — stop unless you are already in the intersection.

question: Who is required to wear seat belts under Alaska law?
options: a:Only passengers under 16 are required.,b:Only front-seat occupants are required.,c:Everyone in a moving vehicle is required to wear a safety belt.
note: Alaska law requires everyone in a motor vehicle to use safety belts; the driver is responsible for passengers under 16.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after a crash, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Wait for law enforcement before moving the vehicle.,b:Never move your vehicle under any circumstances.,c:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.
note: After a minor collision, move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the road if it is safe to do so, while still identifying yourself and rendering assistance.

question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Rely only on the left side mirror.,b:Look quickly over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,d:Turn on your hazard lights first.
note: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure no vehicle is hidden from mirror view.

question: When interacting with pedestrians, a driver must:
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian is aware of their vehicle before proceeding.,b:Always yield the right-of-way,c:Yield only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.,d:Require pedestrians to yield to vehicles.
note: Drivers must do everything possible to avoid striking pedestrians and must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians even if the pedestrian is not following the law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a driver's left arm extended upward indicate?
options: a:The driver intends to turn left.,b:The driver intends to turn right.,c:The driver plans to stop.
note: When a driver's left arm is extended upward, it signals an intention to turn right.

question: How should you position your wheels when parking downhill on a two-way street?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the left away from the curb.,b:Keep the wheels pointed straight ahead.,c:Turn your wheels to the right toward the curb.
note: When parked facing downhill, turn the wheels sharply toward the curb so that if the vehicle rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer is directing traffic at an intersection where the signal is working, whose directions should you follow?
options: a:Honk to get the officer’s attention.,b:Follow the officer’s directions.,c:Follow the traffic light signals.
note: When an officer is directing traffic, their instructions take precedence over traffic signals; drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey the officer.

question: Which statement describes distracted driving?
options: a:It is very uncommon.,b:It is extremely risky behavior that endangers everyone on the road.,c:It is harmless in light traffic.,d:It is only a problem for new drivers.
note: Distracted driving puts drivers, passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other road users at risk and should be avoided.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you always do when turning or changing lanes?
options: a:Signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.,b:Signal only if there is visible traffic.,c:Signal only when driving at night.
note: You must always signal before turning or changing lanes to communicate your intentions to other road users.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:That is parked on the shoulder of the road with no one in it.,b:When it approaches you,c:If you are both driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
note: On two-lane roads, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights and/or extends its stop arm to load or unload children.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a driver's left arm and hand extended downward signal?
options: a:The driver intends to turn right.,b:The driver intends to stop.,c:The driver intends to turn left.
note: A left arm extended downward indicates the driver plans to stop or slow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which of the following should you not do?
options: a:Check your side and rearview mirrors.,b:Give a turn signal to indicate your intentions.,c:Fail to check for drivers who may be moving into the same lane as you.
note: Always check mirrors, signal, and look for other drivers who might also be entering the same lane to avoid collisions.

question: When you see an approaching vehicle with flashing red or blue lights, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down and drive with caution.,c:Drive to the nearest intersection and stop.
note: Yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping until the vehicle has passed.

question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Yes, it decreases BAC.,b:No, it has no effect on BAC.,c:It cancels the alcohol effect.,d:It speeds up alcohol elimination.
note: Coffee or other measures may make you more alert but do not reduce BAC; only time decreases BAC and renders you sober.

question: What are the consequences of refusing a requested chemical test by law enforcement?
options: a:The DMV will revoke your driving privileges and 10 points will be added to your license.,b:You will only receive a warning.,c:There are no administrative consequences.
note: Refusing chemical testing results in DMV action to revoke driving privileges and points added to your record; it can also result in criminal charges.

question: What do downward-pointing triangular road signs usually indicate?
options: a:School zones ahead.,b:Yield to other traffic or pedestrians.,c:Construction zones.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is a yield sign—give right-of-way and proceed only when safe.

question: On which surfaces does your vehicle require a longer stopping distance?
options: a:On paved highways.,b:On a wet or icy road.,c:When driving at night.
note: Stopping distances increase on wet or icy roads and on surfaces covered in loose gravel or stones, so reduce speed and allow extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if an intersection ahead is blocked by traffic?
options: a:Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.,b:Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.,c:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it; blocking the intersection is illegal and causes congestion.

question: If you turn onto a two-lane road that is divided by a broken yellow line, what does that tell you about the road?
options: a:The road is under repair.,b:Traffic travels in two directions (a two-way road).,c:It is a one-way road.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates opposing traffic; it indicates a two‑way road where passing is permitted when safe.

question: If a traffic signal shows a green arrow together with a red light, what movement is allowed?
options: a:You must wait for a solid green light to move in any direction.,b:You may proceed straight ahead only.,c:You may proceed only in the direction indicated by the green arrow.
note: A green arrow with a red light permits movement only in the arrow direction, and only when the intersection is clear.

question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do to increase safety?
options: a:Drive as you would on dry roads.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Use alternate routes.
note: Increase following distance because stopping takes longer on slippery surfaces; avoid sudden speed or steering changes.

question: Under what circumstances may you cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving truck.,b:To pass another car.,c:To turn into a driveway.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may only cross them to make a left turn into or from a driveway, alley, or to enter/exit a highway where allowed.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, when must you pull over and stop?
options: a:Regardless of your direction.,b:Only if it is following you.,c:Only if it is approaching you from the opposite direction.
note: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop for emergency vehicles with flashing lights, whether they are approaching from ahead or behind.

question: If you miss your exit on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Roll down your window and ask someone for directions.,b:Get off at the next exit and safely return to the missed exit.,c:Stop and make a U-turn on the shoulder.
note: Do not back up or try to turn around on the highway. Proceed to the next exit and safely turn around to return to the exit you missed.

question: How can you best avoid the risk of alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Tell people you won't drink if offered.,c:Call a taxi after you start drinking.
note: The only reliable way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you begin drinking that you will not drive.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:Only when following a motorcycle.,b:Only when exiting an expressway.,c:When following a large vehicle that blocks your view of the road ahead.
note: Increase following distance when your vision is blocked by a large vehicle, in bad weather, heavy traffic, and other less-than-ideal conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are about to miss your highway exit, you should:
options: a:Signal,b:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit ramp.,c:Stop in the lane and wait for a gap to reverse course.,d:Continue to the next exit and leave the highway safely.
note: If you miss your exit, stay on the freeway and use the next exit rather than making dangerous lane changes or reversing on the highway.

question: Which actions help you drive safely at night?
options: a:Make sure your headlights are working properly.,b:Not drive if you are tired.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night, ensure headlights are functioning, avoid driving when tired, and increase following distance to improve safety.

question: If your turn signals fail, how should you indicate a turn?
options: a:Use your horn,b:Use hand signals,c:Use your headlights
note: When turn signals are not working, use standard hand signals to indicate turns or lane changes.

question: What do double solid yellow centerlines indicate?
options: a:A residential district is ahead.,b:A dangerous curve is ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate that passing is prohibited from either direction.

question: Which passing rule is correct?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet and make sure no oncoming traffic before passing.,b:When passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car before returning to your lane.,c:Use mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing left.,d:None of the above.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes. Also check mirrors and blind spots and return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before turning must you signal your intention?
options: a:50 feet,b:100 feet,c:200 feet
note: You must display a hand or mechanical turn signal for at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes; signal earlier at higher speeds.

question: If you stop along the road at night, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Use only parking lights.,b:Use only high beams so others see you.,c:Turn off all lights to avoid glare.,d:Leave low-beam headlights on and use emergency flashers.
note: If you stop at night, keep your low beams on and turn on hazard flashers so other road users can see your vehicle.

question: After passing a vehicle on a two-lane road (one lane each direction), when should you return to the driving lane?
options: a:Remain in the left lane if planning to turn left.,b:When there is enough room between you and the passed vehicle.,c:Immediately,d:Only after signaling for 500 feet.
note: On a two-lane roadway, return to the right side when there is sufficient space between you and the vehicle you passed.

question: About how long does it take, on average, for the effects of one 12‑ounce beer to be processed?
options: a:One hour.,b:45 minutes.,c:30 minutes.
note: On average, it takes about one hour for the body to metabolize one standard drink, though individual factors vary.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You will not see the road markings.,b:It increases your fuel efficiency.,c:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly.,d:You might miss the vehicle's signals.
note: Following too closely reduces your stopping time if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly and increases crash risk.

question: If someone has been drinking, what will help them overcome the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Only the passage of time will reduce alcohol impairment.,b:Hot coffee will sober them up quickly.,c:Fresh air will remove the alcohol from their system.
note: Nothing speeds the elimination of alcohol from the body—only time will reduce impairment.

question: When approaching pedestrians on the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Only if they are in marked crosswalks.,b:Yield and be ready to stop as they walk or cross the roadway.,c:Only if a traffic light is yellow or red.,d:Only if they signal you to stop.
note: Slow down, yield, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians who are walking on or crossing the roadway. Always yield to pedestrians on the roadway even if they are not following right-of-way laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light has the same meaning as what sign?
options: a:A yield sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A solid red light.
note: A flashing red signal is treated the same as a stop sign: come to a complete stop and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat posted advisory or speed restriction signs in poor road conditions?
options: a:They may be ignored in rainy,b:They are only recommendations and do not apply in adverse weather.,c:Reduce speed below the posted advisory when conditions make it unsafe to follow it.
note: Advisory speeds are recommended maximums for normal conditions; in rain, snow, ice, or other poor conditions, you should reduce speed below the advisory as needed for safety.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your bloodstream, what happens to your abilities?
options: a:Your judgment improves.,b:Your reaction times slow down.,c:Your metabolism speeds up.
note: As blood alcohol concentration increases, reaction time slows and judgment and coordination deteriorate.

question: If you are in traffic crossing a railroad track with no gates or signals, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,b:You have space to get completely across the tracks without stopping.,c:You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
note: Ensure there is enough room on the far side of the tracks for your vehicle before entering; never stop on the tracks or attempt to pass other vehicles while crossing.

question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Your body weight.,b:How much you drink.,c:The time between drinks.,d:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.
note: BAC is affected by how much you drink, your weight, and the time between drinks; the type of beverage does not change BAC.

question: You are presumed to be driving under the influence if your BAC is at least:
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.02 percent.,c:0.10 percent.,d:0.08 percent.
note: Legal consequences apply when your blood alcohol concentration is 0.08% or higher. Driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol is a serious offense.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to stop or park along the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:If you turn on your emergency flashers.,b:To consult a map or directions.,c:Only in an emergency.
note: Parking on a freeway shoulder is prohibited except in emergencies.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:High-beam headlights.,c:Low-beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped).
note: In fog, use low-beam headlights (and fog lights if available); high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: When backing up, what is the recommended way to look?
options: a:Turn your head and body to look out the rear window.,b:Use only the rearview mirror.,c:Open the door and step out to look.,d:Turn on your headlights and back using mirrors only.
note: When backing, do not depend only on mirrors. Turn your head and body to the right and look out the rear window to check for obstacles.

question: When you hear the siren of a fire engine behind you, you must:
options: a:Continue at the same speed to clear the way.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Drive with your hazard lights on.,d:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: Upon hearing an emergency vehicle’s siren, pull to the nearest curb or side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: What do round road signs typically indicate?
options: a:Construction ahead.,b:An upcoming railroad crossing.,c:A no-passing zone.,d:A school zone.
note: Round signs warn of railroad crossings ahead; approach such areas with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, and that vehicle is to your right, you should:
options: a:Drive into the intersection and force the other to stop.,b:Speed up to beat the other vehicle.,c:Honk to assert the right-of-way.,d:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
note: At uncontrolled intersections, yield to vehicles on your right when you arrive at the same time; proceed only when it’s safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-way, two-lane street, you cannot pass safely unless which condition is met?
options: a:You are traveling below the posted speed limit.,b:You are able to clearly see the road ahead and can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,c:Your vehicle is small enough to pass quickly.
note: Do not pass unless you have clear visibility of the road ahead and can return to your lane before encountering oncoming traffic.

question: If your vehicle's power steering fails while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, and drive to a safe area to stop.,b:Turn off the ignition immediately and continue steering.,c:Open your hood and stop in the lane of travel.
note: Loss of power steering increases steering effort; slow down, steer carefully to a safe area, and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection that has a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After stopping at least 20 feet prior to the intersection.,b:After slowing down enough to see cross traffic but not stopping.,c:After coming to a complete stop before entering the intersection and verifying it is safe to proceed.
note: Where a stop sign is present but no line or marked crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection and proceed only when safe.

question: What colors are used on warning signs for upcoming hazards?
options: a:Black letters or symbols on a white background,b:White letters or symbols on a blue background,c:Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
note: General warning signs use black symbols or lettering on a yellow background; work zone warnings use orange with black symbols.

question: When the road is marked with a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line with the broken line adjacent to your lane, you may:
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If traffic is clear.,c:If you are on an expressway.
note: If the broken yellow line is on your side, you may cross to pass when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe to do so.

question: An orange triangular sign with red borders displayed on the rear of a vehicle indicates what?
options: a:The vehicle is a slow-moving vehicle.,b:The vehicle is broken down.,c:The vehicle is a school bus.
note: The orange triangle with red borders marks a slow-moving vehicle, typically one that cannot exceed about 25 mph.

question: When you approach a steady green arrow signal, what are you allowed to do?
options: a:Make the turn indicated by the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Merge into the lane indicated by the arrow.,c:Slow to a stop if it is safe to do so.
note: A steady green arrow allows you to turn in the arrow’s direction if you are in the proper lane; yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you should:
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way to traffic you are entering.,b:Always stop before proceeding.,c:Yield only to traffic on the right.,d:Accelerate to merge quickly.
note: A yield sign means slow down and give right-of-way to vehicles in the roadway you are entering; stop if necessary.

question: Where are stop lines (solid white lines) painted on the roadway?
options: a:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.,b:In curves and on hills.,c:Next to churches and schools.
note: Stop lines are painted across lanes to indicate where vehicles must stop at intersections and crosswalks.

question: How does night driving compare to daytime driving?
options: a:It is neither more nor less dangerous.,b:It is more dangerous.,c:It is less dangerous.
note: Driving at night is more hazardous — visibility is reduced, glare can blind drivers temporarily, and there may be more fatigued or impaired drivers on the road.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which side should pedestrians use?
options: a:Same side of the road on which traffic is moving.,b:Side of the road which has the lightest traffic.,c:Side of the road facing oncoming traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk on the left side of the road, facing oncoming traffic, so they can see approaching vehicles.

question: Under what circumstances may you drive around a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:If the gate appears to be malfunctioning.,b:If you think you have enough time to cross before it lowers fully.,c:Never — do not drive around lowered gates.
note: It is against the law and extremely dangerous to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates; remain stopped until the gates are raised.

question: Within what distance of an oncoming vehicle should you dim your high beams?
options: a:400 feet,b:500 feet,c:200 feet
note: Dim high beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: What should you do to maximize safety when backing your vehicle?
options: a:Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.,b:Check behind the vehicle before you get into the driver's seat.,c:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.
note: Backing requires extra caution because drivers have limited rear visibility. Before getting into the vehicle to back up, walk around and check for children and small objects behind it.

question: Statistics show alcohol is:
options: a:Rarely involved in any traffic crashes.,b:Involved in almost half of all traffic crashes that result in death.,c:The cause of all traffic crashes.
note: Alcohol is a significant factor in fatal crashes; in Alaska, alcohol is involved in close to 45% of traffic deaths.

question: How does eating or drinking while driving affect driving?
options: a:It distracts you and impairs lane control and vehicle handling.,b:It helps you focus on driving.,c:It has no effect on driving.,d:It makes you a better driver.
note: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving diverts hands and eyes from driving and increases the risk of errors and collisions.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing that only has a crossbuck and no gates or lights, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until a flagger clears you to cross in all cases.,b:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.,c:Turn down your radio to listen for a train but otherwise proceed.
note: Approach track crossings carefully and only proceed when you are certain no train is coming from either direction.

question: Why must you use extra caution around a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They are a police officer.,b:They are signaling for a taxi.,c:They are likely blind and need right-of-way and assistance.
note: A person using a white cane or guide dog is blind or visually impaired; you must yield and be prepared to stop to prevent injury.

question: What is the minimum jail term for a first-time DUI conviction in Alaska?
options: a:Three days,b:10 days,c:20 hours
note: A first DUI conviction carries mandatory jail time — the minimum mandatory penalty is three days in jail, plus fines and fees.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should:
options: a:Sound your horn to warn others.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Check rearview and side mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots.,d:Reduce your speed to below 10 mph.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to ensure no one occupies your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street, where should your vehicle end up?
options: a:Be in the center of the street.,b:Be in the right lane of the street.,c:Be in the left lane of the one-way street.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the lane nearest the lane you came from (the left lane).

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do with the steering wheel?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel in the direction of the skid.,b:Overcorrect immediately.,c:Turn the steering wheel into oncoming traffic.
note: If your vehicle skids, remain calm and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.

question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Cars overheat more quickly at night.,b:It is more likely to be raining at night.,c:Visibility is reduced in the dark.
note: Reduced visibility at night limits your field of vision; use headlights and reduce speed to maintain stopping distance within sight range.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what is the correct merging technique?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp,b:Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.,c:Accelerate to match the speed of traffic and merge when a gap is available.
note: Use the acceleration lane to reach highway speed, signal, find a gap, and merge smoothly with traffic.

question: Which statement about work zones is correct?
options: a:Drivers do not need to slow down in work zones.,b:They are marked with black-and-white signs.,c:Work zones may be stationary or moving and require extra caution.
note: Work zones can be stationary or involve moving operations (striping, mowing), are marked with orange signs, and require drivers to slow down and pay attention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,c:Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.
note: If you're impeding traffic on a two-lane, two-way road, pull off the road at a safe place to allow others to pass.

question: What do work zone signs generally indicate?
options: a:Less than ideal conditions are present for driving.,b:You must immediately stop and back up.,c:It is summer.
note: Work zone signs are orange and warn that road work is being done on or near the roadway; exercise extra caution in these areas.

question: A driver's license may be suspended for which of the following reasons?
options: a:Driving in violation of license restrictions.,b:Operating an uninsured vehicle.,c:Repeated violations of motor vehicle laws.
note: Accumulating repeated violations of motor vehicle laws can lead to suspension or revocation of driving privileges.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:
options: a:Have improved reaction time.,b:Are more aware of the risks they are taking.,c:Drive better because they are more careful.,d:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies and the vehicle.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that impairs judgment, vision, reaction time, and coordination; drivers under the influence lack sufficient control to operate a vehicle safely.

question: If you start to drive in rainy conditions, you should:
options: a:Drive at the posted maximum speed.,b:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,c:Slow down and turn on your headlights.,d:Pull over immediately to the shoulder.
note: When it begins to rain reduce speed, turn on headlights so others can see you, and if visibility becomes very poor, pull off the road safely.

question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:At your dashboard instruments.,b:At your right-side mirror.,c:Over your left shoulder.
note: To check blind spots when changing lanes left, glance over your left shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

question: Which actions can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allowing extra travel time.,b:Using proper turn signals.,c:Obeying posted speed limits.
note: To reduce aggressive driving incidents, allow extra travel time, use proper turn signals and obey speed limits.

question: How must drivers treat traffic signs and pavement markings?
options: a:Must be followed only when there is other traffic.,b:Are merely suggestions.,c:Must always be obeyed.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and must be obeyed at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What steps should you take when changing lanes on a highway?
options: a:Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.,b:Check your rearview and outside mirrors.,c:Signal a lane change.
note: Always signal, check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to verify your blind spot before changing lanes.

question: Before passing another vehicle on the road, you should:
options: a:Signal only if someone is behind you.,b:Never signal to avoid confusion.,c:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your intent.,d:Signal only after you begin passing.
note: Signal early so others will know your intentions in advance; signaling just before or after is unsafe.

question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Accelerate quickly.,b:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.,c:Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
note: After a school bus unloads children, watch carefully for pedestrians near the roadway before resuming travel.

question: When must you submit proof of insurance to the DMV after being in a crash?
options: a:If the crash results in personal injury, death, or property damage of $501 or more.,b:Only if property damage exceeds $1,000.,c:Only if property damage exceeds $2,000.
note: If a crash results in bodily injury, death, or property damage of $501 or more, you must provide proof of insurance to the DMV within 15 days.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Signaling your intentions before turning or changing lanes is:
options: a:Necessary only during the maneuver itself.,b:A required driving habit and good practice.,c:Required only if other traffic is present.,d:Discouraged on multilane roads.
note: You must signal in advance (at least 100 feet) before changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb to inform other road users of your plans.

question: If a transit bus signals it will re-enter traffic after a stop, you must:
options: a:Honking to warn the driver.,b:Move into the lane beside it immediately.,c:Yield to the bus and allow it to re-enter.,d:Speed up to pass the bus first.
note: You must yield to a transit vehicle that is signaling to pull back onto the roadway after stopping to pick up or drop off passengers; change lanes, slow, or stop to let it merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper top-to-bottom order of lights on a vertically-arranged traffic signal?
options: a:Green,b:Red,c:Red at the top
note: On a vertical traffic signal the order from top to bottom is red, yellow, then green.

question: How should you scan the road to prepare for upcoming hazards?
options: a:Stare straight ahead only.,b:Keep your left foot lightly on the brake.,c:Continuously scan the entire road and its sides.,d:Only check your mirrors periodically.
note: Search and identify potential problems before you get to them by scanning far ahead and the sides of the road rather than staring at the center of the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What greatly increases stopping distances and the severity of crashes?
options: a:High speeds,b:Slow speeds,c:Night driving
note: Higher speeds increase the distance needed to stop and raise the force of impact in a collision, making crashes more severe.

question: If you meet a school bus stopped with flashing lights on the opposite side of a divided highway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the bus lights stop flashing.,b:Turn around and use another route.,c:You may continue driving because the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.
note: If the school bus is stopped with flashers on the opposite side of a divided highway, drivers may continue driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a solid yellow line?
options: a:To pass traffic moving in the same direction.,b:At any time.,c:Only when making a turn (for example, into a driveway or side road).
note: Broken lines may be crossed to pass; solid yellow lines generally may only be crossed when making turns into driveways or side roads, not to pass.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what actions should you take?
options: a:Slow down and look for a train.,b:Be prepared to stop.,c:All of the above (slow down, look, and be ready to stop).
note: If you see signs indicating a railroad crossing, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. If lights are flashing or gates are down, stop 15 to 50 feet from the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the standard speed limit posted for many school zones in Alaska?
options: a:10 mph.,b:20 mph.,c:25 mph.
note: The typical school zone speed limit in Alaska is 20 mph; always drive cautiously where children are present.

question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down once you have moved onto the exit ramp.,b:Slow down well before reaching the ramp.,c:Maintain highway speed while on the ramp.
note: Do not reduce speed on the mainline before moving onto the exit ramp; slow down after you are on the ramp where it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close to a fire hydrant is it illegal to park?
options: a:30 feet,b:15 feet,c:25 feet
note: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant to ensure emergency access.

question: If your tire suddenly blows out while driving, how should you respond?
options: a:Slam on your brakes immediately.,b:Keep driving at the same speed until you reach a service station.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly
note: If a tire blows out, grip the wheel tightly, gradually reduce speed by easing off the accelerator, and steer to a safe stop—avoid sudden braking.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the left side of the road.,b:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,c:Toward the right side of the road.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid being blinded by oncoming high beams while maintaining enough view to stay on course.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why must you adjust your driving speed?
options: a:Other traffic.,b:Weather conditions.,c:All of the above.,d:Existing road conditions.
note: Adjust speed to accommodate road, weather, time of day and traffic conditions; reduce speed when conditions are less than ideal.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Flash your lights at them.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.,c:Never pass them under any circumstances.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots to the sides and rear; avoid lingering beside them and do not tailgate.

question: What can result from combining alcohol with other drugs?
options: a:Complete cancelation of effects.,b:A guaranteed cure of symptoms.,c:An increase in the effects of both substances.,d:A decrease in effects of both.
note: Combining alcohol with drugs can enhance the effects of both, increasing impairment and danger when driving.

question: If a crossing guard directs traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.,b:Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.,c:Copy surrounding traffic even if it conflicts with the guard.
note: Obey crossing guards and law enforcement in school zones; slow down and use caution as directed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Drive carefully through the intersection.,b:Stop and wait for the light to change.,c:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution; slow down, watch for hazards and cross traffic, and continue when safe.

question: If your car begins to skid, which way should you steer?
options: a:In the opposite direction of the skid.,b:To keep the front wheels straight.,c:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
note: If the vehicle skids, steer in the direction you want to go, and when it straightens, correct the wheel position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, you should:
